sentences.text:
Rohit Kumar .....Applicant(s) Versus State of U.P. .....Opposite Party(s) Counsel for
Applicant(s) :
Brajesh Kumar Singh Counsel for Opposite Party(s) :
G.A. Hon'Ble Krishan Pahal, J. 1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Brajesh Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 208 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B, 504 of IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Narkhi, District Firozabad, during the pendency of trial.
4.
Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The applicant is the husband of the deceased person and he has nothing to do with the said offence.
The FIR is delayed and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
5. Learned counsel has next stated that the deceased was seeing the marriage procession in the village and had subsequently died under mysterious circumstances.
The applicant himself was present in the marriage ceremony.
6. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 20.05.2023 and only one witness has been examined to date.
There is no likelihood of early conclusion of trial in near future.
The applicant is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail

,
he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.
8. This Court had called for a report regarding the status of trial and in compliance thereof, a report dated 01.08.2025 has been submitted by the concerned trial court.
As per the said report, PW-1 has been examined to date.
9. The Supreme Court in its latest judgement passed in SLP (Crl.) Nos.10455-10456/2025 Ramnath Mishra @ Ramanath Mishra v. Central Bureau of Investigation

sentences.text: 1 liberty must be addressed with utmost speed by Courts.
The accused had already been incarcerated for more than three and a half years, in the instant and connected matters.

Releasing accused on bail due to excessive delays by the High Court in deciding his application also took into account lengthy pre-trial confinement, emphasizing speedy decision-making for matters of personal liberty.

10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record and taking into consideration the period of incarceration i.e. two years and three months undergone by the applicant, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant- Rohit Kumar, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii) The applicant shall not pressurise/intimidate with the prosecution witnesses.
iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
12. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

13. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

(Krishan Pahal,J.) September 2, 2025 Sumit S  Rohit Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87321893/
